title: Maximise Items With a Cooler-Bag Cost
statement:
You are shopping with a budget of `B`. There are `n` items, and item `i` has a price `cost[i]` and a type `type[i]` that is either `0` or `1`. Each item can be bought **at most once**.

Items of type `1` must be carried in a reusable cooler bag. If you buy **at least one** item of type `1`, you must also pay a one-time cooler-bag cost `C`, no matter how many type `1` items you buy. Buying only type `0` items costs nothing extra.

Choose a set of items whose total price (plus `C` if the set contains a type `1` item) does not exceed `B`. Print the **maximum number of items** you can buy. Buying nothing is allowed, so the answer can be `0`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains three integers `n`, `B` and `C`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `cost[i]` and `type[i]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of items that can be bought.

examples.explanation: Without the cooler bag you can buy the type 0 items costing 2 and 4 (total 6); the item costing 6 would exceed 10, so that gives 2 items. If you pay the cooler-bag cost 3, you have 7 left and can buy the items costing 1, 2 and 3 (total 6), for 3 items and a total of 9.
The cooler bag costs more than the whole budget, so type 1 items are out of reach. Buy the two type 0 items for 5.
Paying 5 for the cooler bag leaves 15, enough for the items costing 4, 5 and 6 (total 15). Only buying the type 0 item gives just 1 item.

hints: If the price of every item were fixed and there were no cooler bag, which items would you buy to maximise the count?
Split the problem into two cases: you buy no type 1 item (budget B, type 0 items only), or you pay C up front and then every item is available with budget B - C.

In the second case, just greedily take the cheapest items from the whole list. If that selection happens to contain no type 1 item, it is still no better than case one, so taking the maximum of the two cases is safe.
